evidence.claim: IMF said India’s authorities responded to post-pandemic shocks with fiscal policy measures to support vulnerable groups and with front-loaded monetary tightening to address elevated inflation.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation with India
evidence.excerpt: IMF said India’s authorities responded to post-pandemic shocks with fiscal policy measures to support vulnerable groups and with front-loaded monetary tightening to address elevated inflation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF Article IV release with explicit assessment of policy response and fiscal/monetary actions in 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about FY2022/23 and the 2022 policy year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Modi-led Union government, though the monetary tightening was executed by the RBI rather than Modi personally.
contrary_evidence: The IMF also warned that inflation remained high and that public debt risks had increased.

evidence.claim: IMF credited India’s digital public infrastructure with rapid deployment of support, efficient payments, and increased financial inclusion, while saying narrowings of the digital divide, female labor force participation, youth unemployment, and informality remained important issues.
evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation with India
evidence.excerpt: IMF credited India’s digital public infrastructure with rapid deployment of support, efficient payments, and increased financial inclusion, while saying narrowings of the digital divide, female labor force participation, youth unemployment, and informality remained important issues.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Same IMF release, but this claim is distinct because it covers digital infrastructure and distributional labor-market weaknesses.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to 2022 economic governance and distribution.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Modi-era policy architecture, but digital infrastructure was built through multiple ministries and prior years.
contrary_evidence: The IMF explicitly said female labor force participation, youth unemployment, and informality still needed progress.

evidence.claim: The World Bank approved a $750 million DPL to support reforms that leverage private sector investment in infrastructure, small businesses, and green finance markets.
evidence.title: World Bank Approves $750 Million Loan to India to Catalyze Private Financing and Support Economic Growth
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank approved a $750 million DPL to support reforms that leverage private sector investment in infrastructure, small businesses, and green finance markets.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank press release describing the exact policy loan and reform package.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Government of India under Modi, though the loan reflects lender endorsement of a broader reform package.
contrary_evidence: The page also notes large infrastructure and MSME finance gaps, so the loan addresses a shortfall rather than proving prior success.

evidence.claim: The operation supported issuing India’s first sovereign green bonds and improving access to credit for MSMEs and women entrepreneurs through de-risking and guarantee mechanisms.
evidence.title: World Bank Approves $750 Million Loan to India to Catalyze Private Financing and Support Economic Growth
evidence.excerpt: The operation supported issuing India’s first sovereign green bonds and improving access to credit for MSMEs and women entrepreneurs through de-risking and guarantee mechanisms.
evidence.source_locator: bullet points 'Developing the markets for green finance' and 'Improving access to credit for MSMEs and women entrepreneurs'
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary lender description of the supported reforms and target beneficiaries.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2022 reform design and implementation support.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government-level attribution under Modi, with implementation shared across finance, banking, and sector ministries.
contrary_evidence: The same source frames these as reforms to fill financing gaps, so it does not show that access problems were already solved.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said India’s economy was resilient and relatively well positioned to weather global spillovers compared with most emerging markets, despite a deteriorating external environment.
evidence.title: India Better Positioned to Navigate Global Headwinds Than Other Major Emerging Economies: New World Bank Report
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said India’s economy was resilient and relatively well positioned to weather global spillovers compared with most emerging markets, despite a deteriorating external environment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank report summary with an explicit macro assessment for late 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about the 2022 macro year and growth outlook.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Modi’s government, but the report also emphasizes external shocks and structural conditions.
contrary_evidence: The same report says the external environment would still weigh on growth prospects and require continued vigilance.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said policy reforms and prudent regulatory measures improved resilience, while market borrowings improved transparency and credibility of fiscal policy and inflation targeting helped monetary credibility.
evidence.title: India Better Positioned to Navigate Global Headwinds Than Other Major Emerging Economies: New World Bank Report
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said policy reforms and prudent regulatory measures improved resilience, while market borrowings improved transparency and credibility of fiscal policy and inflation targeting helped monetary credibility.
evidence.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Policy reforms and prudent regulatory measures have also played a key role'
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank assessment with specific mechanisms named.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly attributable to the Modi government and the RBI framework, but not to one office-holder alone.
contrary_evidence: The same passage still implies continued macro risks and a need for caution.

evidence.claim: PRS summarized the 2022-23 Union Budget as raising capital expenditure by 24.5 percent and setting the fiscal deficit at 6.4 percent of GDP.
evidence.title: Union Budget 2022-23 Analysis
evidence.excerpt: PRS summarized the 2022-23 Union Budget as raising capital expenditure by 24.5 percent and setting the fiscal deficit at 6.4 percent of GDP.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent budget analysis grounded in official budget documents with exact fiscal figures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Modi government through the Union Budget, though execution depended on ministries and state uptake.
contrary_evidence: A 6.4 percent fiscal deficit is still a large deficit, so this is not simple prudence without qualification.

evidence.claim: PRS reported larger allocations for Road Transport and Highways, Education, Health and Family Welfare, Jal Shakti, PM-KISAN, MGNREGS, National Education Mission, National Health Mission, and welfare of women and children in the 2022-23 budget.
evidence.title: Union Budget 2022-23 Analysis
evidence.excerpt: PRS reported larger allocations for Road Transport and Highways, Education, Health and Family Welfare, Jal Shakti, PM-KISAN, MGNREGS, National Education Mission, National Health Mission, and welfare of women and children in the 2022-23 budget.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent budget analysis of sector and scheme allocations with exact numbers.
evidence.period_fit: Directly 2022 budget allocations affecting households and productivity.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Modi government’s budget priorities, though spending outcomes depend on implementation by line ministries and states.
contrary_evidence: Some other social allocations were flat or fell, so the budget mix was selective rather than uniformly expansionary.

evidence.claim: PRS noted that the budget linked transport and logistics projects to PM GatiShakti, created the DESH Stack for skilling and job matching, and planned sovereign green bonds for green infrastructure.
evidence.title: Union Budget 2022-23 Analysis
evidence.excerpt: PRS noted that the budget linked transport and logistics projects to PM GatiShakti, created the DESH Stack for skilling and job matching, and planned sovereign green bonds for green infrastructure.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent budget analysis summarizing multiple named policy instruments in one budget package.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Modi government’s economic agenda, with operational delivery spread across ministries.
contrary_evidence: These were plans and framework choices; the source does not itself prove successful execution in 2022.

evidence.claim: The Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended PMGKAY for another six months to September 2022, adding free foodgrains for poor and vulnerable households.
evidence.title: Centre extends Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) for another six months (April-September, 2022)
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended PMGKAY for another six months to September 2022, adding free foodgrains for poor and vulnerable households.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraph and scheme summary in the PIB release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Cabinet release announcing the extension and naming Modi as the chair of the Cabinet decision.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Modi as Cabinet chair.
contrary_evidence: The scheme was an extension of a pandemic-era program, so it reflects continuation as much as new initiative.

evidence.claim: The Union Cabinet approved another extension of PMGKAY for October to December 2022, providing five kilograms of free grain per person per month to NFSA beneficiaries.
evidence.title: Centre extends Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Ann Yojana (PMGKAY) for another three months (October 2022-December 2022)
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The Union Cabinet approved another extension of PMGKAY for October to December 2022, providing five kilograms of free grain per person per month to NFSA beneficiaries.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraph and scheme summary in the PIB release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Cabinet release with explicit coverage of the 2022 extension.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Modi as Cabinet chair.
contrary_evidence: Again, this is continuation of an existing safety-net rather than evidence of a new structural reform.

evidence.claim: The Ministry of Rural Development said that in FY2021-22 MGNREGS had completed 83.82 lakh works and had 133.09 lakh works ongoing, while remaining a demand-driven wage-employment program.
evidence.title: Study to Assess the Impact of MGNREGS
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The Ministry of Rural Development said that in FY2021-22 MGNREGS had completed 83.82 lakh works and had 133.09 lakh works ongoing, while remaining a demand-driven wage-employment program.
evidence.source_locator: opening lines and FY2021-22 performance summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry release with concrete implementation statistics.
evidence.period_fit: Covers the fiscal year ending in 2022 and thus the target year period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Modi-led central government, though state execution is crucial for delivery.
contrary_evidence: The release is descriptive of works and does not show how well wages or job quality translated into long-term gains.

evidence.claim: The central government released ₹86,912 crore in GST compensation to states to help them manage resources and continue capital expenditure.
evidence.title: Centre Clears Entire GST Compensation Due Till Date (31ST MAY, 2022)
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The central government released ₹86,912 crore in GST compensation to states to help them manage resources and continue capital expenditure.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and table of state-wise breakup
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official central-government fiscal release with a clear statement of funds transferred to states.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi-led central government’s fiscal choices.
contrary_evidence: Compensation payments are important fiscal support, but they also show the Centre was still managing a strained post-GST settlement.

evidence.claim: The government appointed Dr V. Anantha Nageswaran as Chief Economic Advisor, and he assumed charge on the same day.
evidence.title: Appointment of Dr V Anantha Nageswaran as the Chief Economic Advisor
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The government appointed Dr V. Anantha Nageswaran as Chief Economic Advisor, and he assumed charge on the same day.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official appointment notice naming the appointee and the position exactly.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Modi government’s choice of senior economic personnel.
contrary_evidence: One competent appointment does not by itself prove that all economic decisions were technocratic or evidence-based.

evidence.claim: The government appointed economist Suman Bery as Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog, the Prime Minister’s policy think tank, effective May 1, 2022.
evidence.title: NITI Aayog Welcomes Suman Bery as NITI Aayog Vice Chairman
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
evidence.excerpt: The government appointed economist Suman Bery as Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog, the Prime Minister’s policy think tank, effective May 1, 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official appointment release with clear identification of the office and the appointee’s background.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Modi as the head of government and NITI Aayog’s chair.
contrary_evidence: NITI Aayog is advisory, so this says more about advice architecture than direct execution.
